Destinations._comment: Silos is a tenant domain -> dedicated-silo base address map (XD01-289), one entry per Tier-2 pilot tenant provisioned with its own silo deployment. A request whose X-Tenant-Domain header doesn't match any configured entry falls through to Shared, never to another tenant's silo. The one example entry below matches this repo's docker-compose default silo service names. Routes (GatewayRouteCatalog, XD01-384): /api/geoassets/**, /api/ip-billing/**, /api/field-service/** forwarded as they are; /api/v/neutral-operator/** -> NeutralOperator with the prefix rewritten to /api/** (query string kept); every other /api/** plus /wms and /wfs -> GeoAssets (the kernel catch-all, lowest precedence).

NeutralOperator._comment: XD01-384: GeoAssets.NeutralOperator.Server (ADR-001 Phase 7). Rollback of the cut-over: point Shared (and each silo) at the kernel (the GeoAssets destination) and list 'neutral-operator' again in the kernel's GeoAssets:Modules — the kernel-hosted module serves the same /api/workflow routes, so the same /api/v/neutral-operator/** -> /api/** rewrite reaches it. See deploy/neutral-operator/README.md.

Cors._comment: XD01-384: the browser origins (the Blazor Web app) allowed to call the gateway — the same setting, and the same policy (any header, any method), as GeoAssets.Server's. The gateway is the one CORS authority: it answers preflights itself and drops the backends' Access-Control-* response headers.

AzureAdCiam._comment: XD01-398: the Entra External ID (CIAM) tenant whose signing keys validate the bearer token before the rate limiter keys a bucket by its claims — the same Instance/TenantId as GeoAssets.Server's. MetadataAddress overrides the OpenID Connect metadata document, by default {Instance}/{TenantId}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration. All blank (the default): tokens are only decoded, as before XD01-398. Fetched once and cached (refreshed on its own schedule, and on a token signed by an unknown key at most once per refresh interval).

RateLimiting._comment: XD01-214/XD01-393: token buckets at the gateway edge, so one caller's burst (a mobile photo sync, a map pan's tiles) can't degrade the others sharing the clusters. Two policies, each its own bucket per caller — exhausting one never 429s the other: Tiles = the anonymous OGC map traffic (/wms, /wfs), Api = every other request; /healthz is never limited. The caller (partition key), first match wins: the OrganizationIdClaimType claim of the bearer token (org:, unset by default — Entra CIAM emits none; once set, size Api for a whole organization), else its subject oid/sub (sub:), else the client IP (ip:) — the claims count only from a token whose signature, issuer and lifetime validate against the AzureAdCiam tenant's signing keys (XD01-398; audience not checked, nothing is ever rejected for its token — the gateway authorizes nothing), so a forged, expired or unverifiable token keys by the client IP; with AzureAdCiam unset the token is only decoded (a startup warning says so) and a forged one can name another caller's bucket. TokenValidation: ClockSkewSeconds is the lifetime tolerance, MetadataFailureBackoffSeconds how long after a failed signing-key fetch tokens key by IP before the next try. Behind a load balancer, list it in TrustedProxies (IPs) or TrustedNetworks (CIDRs): only their X-Forwarded-For is believed, otherwise the connection's address is the client. Each bucket holds TokenLimit requests and gets TokensPerPeriod back every ReplenishmentPeriodSeconds; a rejected request gets 429 with Retry-After and a problem body (code rate-limit.exceeded). Defaults come from the request-count model of docs/perf/gateway-rate-limits.md (re-measure with tools/GeoAssets.Tools.GatewayLoadProfile). The pre-XD01-393 flat RateLimiting:TokenLimit/TokensPerPeriod/ReplenishmentPeriodSeconds still work and override Api when set.
